CORY READ THIS ITS FOR YOUR HEALTH

The sensation of the inside of your mouth peeling after brushing can be a sign of irritation or damage to the soft tissues in your mouth, often caused by the ingredients in your toothpaste or mouthwash.
 This white, slimy discharge or peeling sensation is frequently linked to toothpastes containing harsh whitening agents, peroxide, or high concentrations of baking soda, which can burn the delicate mucous membranes inside the mouth.
 Products like Crest Pro Health and some Sensodyne formulations have been reported to cause this issue.
 The irritation leads to dead tissue forming a film or peeling layer, which is then expelled during brushing.

Another contributing factor can be brushing too hard or using an improper technique, such as aggressive horizontal strokes, which can damage the gums and cause them to recede or peel.
 It is recommended to brush at a 45-degree angle to the gum line using gentle, circular motions to avoid injuring the gums and enamel.
 Additionally, brushing immediately after consuming acidic foods or drinks can weaken tooth enamel, and brushing while the enamel is softened can cause further damage, potentially leading to a peeling sensation.

If the peeling persists, it may indicate underlying issues such as plaque or tartar buildup, gingivitis, or even early signs of periodontal disease, especially if accompanied by bleeding gums, sensitivity, or discoloration.
 In such cases, a dental consultation is advised to rule out more serious conditions and to receive professional cleaning or treatment.
 To prevent this, consider switching to a toothpaste formulated for sensitive teeth, avoiding harsh ingredients, and waiting at least 15-30 minutes after consuming acidic foods before brushing.

Content:
Hi Cory,
I’m not sure if you’ll read this or not, but it just needed to be said. With everything having happened, I can say for myself and I’m sure that there are plenty of others who will agree, but we as your fans are here for you. It breaks my heart that there are people who are so obsessed with the internet that it’s all they have and that they will see someone who is either enjoying their life or living the life that they created for themselves and will instantly want to bring them down. But, as for myself and everyone who loves you, your videos, your manga, everything, we will be there to lift you up. I may not have been watching you since the beginning, but I have watched enough to know that your videos, personality, humor and smile have become an important part of my day. I’m an artist and having just started a full-time, corporate job doing graphic design for the first time, it has been strenuous. But knowing I can come home, cook up some dinner and put on one of your videos that makes me laugh and smile, I look forward to it almost everyday. I may not understand or know everything that has happened in your life, but what I do know is that I am grateful that you made me smile. When I heard that you released your own manga, I was ecstatic, not just to be able to read it, but the fact that you were able to do something YOU wanted. You had a dream and were both lucky and determined that it came true. Many people do get that chance or even have it, but when I see someone who has a dream and makes it a reality, I can’t help but feel joy for that person because it’s what I wish to do as well. Those who chose to take up time in their day to try and bring you down or say hurtful and hateful things about/to you, it’s their ignorance at fault. They wish to take up the time in their life, which is limited, to be hateful, ignorant, immature creatures that the only thing they have in life is the hatred they have for theirs and how they have not made anything of it. WE LOVE YOU CORY! I wish I could create a piece of art that could bring a smile to your face as your videos have done for me time and time again. You were able to make me smile and no matter what you decide, whatever you wish to do, I will always be grateful for that smile. Because even if it was once, that was more than enough.

Thank you Cory, for the laughs, the smiles, the tears, everything. 

-Emily, proud samurai since 2018

Here are some common reasons your mouth or inner cheeks might peel after brushing your teeth:
	•	Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) in toothpaste

	•	Overbrushing
	•	Brushing too hard can damage the soft tissues inside your mouth.
	•	Mouthwash irritation
	•	Strong alcohol-based or antiseptic mouthwashes can cause tissue sloughing.
	•	Dry mouth
	•	Lack of saliva can make tissues more prone to peeling and irritation.
	•	Desquamation (normal shedding)
	•	Some mild peeling is a normal renewal process for the inner lining of your mouth.
	•	Reaction to whitening products
	•	Peroxides in whitening toothpaste or strips can cause sensitivity and peeling.
